subject: Orbit Analytics — MSA & Order Form: DPA localization questions and SCCs clarification
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbit-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Bianchi <m.bianchi@orbit-analytics.it>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: MSA + DPA redline (Orbit Analytics)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our redline of the MSA and the DPA. There are three items our counsel asked us to surface up front so you can route internally:

1) SCCs: we expect inclusion of the updated EU SCCs and a brief statement on fallback routing if cross-border transfers are needed.
2) Delegation/roles: we propose a tighter controller/processor split and a specific clause that requires processor-to-processor subprocessor notice with 30 days' pre-notice for EU-resident data.
3) Transfer impact addendum: a short appendix detailing how transfers are limited to EU regions unless a Transfer Impact Addendum is executed.

We've highlighted those items in the attached redline and added comments where we think a feasible compromise could be 1) an SCCs exhibit, 2) an approved subprocessor list cadence, and 3) a 90-day transition for any cross-border hosting changes.

Attachments: Orbit_MSA_DPA_redline_20260618.docx

Can you confirm who is best to coordinate answers from your side? We're on a fairly tight procurement timeline — target signature by July 2 if possible.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations
Orbit Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: MSA + DPA redline (Orbit Analytics)

Monica, Ben — forwarding Orbit's redline (attached). Key asks from their counsel are in Elena's note below. Please treat this as priority: procurement wants to know if we can hit a July 2 signature target or whether we need to request more runway.

Suggested split of work:
- Monica: lead on DPA/SCCs responses and proposed language for controller/processor roles.
- Ben: coordinate procurement timeline, commercial concessions (if any), and confirm whether we can commit to the 90-day transition or need an exception.

Action items:
- Monica: can you review the redline and put together a one-page recommended stance with negotiated language snippets by COB Mon 22 Jun?
- Ben: please confirm internal owner for order form finalization and whether we need legal/commercial exec signoff if we agree to a transfer addendum window.

I'll loop back to Orbit with a consolidated response. If anyone prefers a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning, say so now — otherwise I'll assume asynchronous coordination.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbit-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:47:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA + DPA redline (Orbit Analytics)

Karthik/Ben — reviewed the redline and added inline comments in the document (I'll upload the cleaned snippet to the Drive link). High-level recommendations:

1) SCCs: we accept adding the updated EU SCCs as an exhibit. We'll propose a narrow fallback clause: transfers outside the EU only if (a) customer executes the Transfer Impact Addendum, or (b) we route to a compatible region with customer notice. This preserves our routing flexibility while meeting their ask.

2) Roles & Delegation: we will not accept a blanket 30-day pre-notice requirement for subprocessors; instead propose: prior notice for material subprocessor additions (security-affecting/hosting changes) and quarterly published subprocessor list. For EU-resident data, commit to notification plus 30 days' opportunity for customer to object to a material change — not an automatic block.

3) Transfer Impact Addendum: we can agree to a short appendix that limits cross-border hosting by default to EU-only, with a documented process and 90-day transition for approved exceptions. This should be a customer-option appendix rather than an immutable default, to avoid operational lock.

I've attached the proposed SCCs snippet (proposed_sccs_snippet.txt) and an internal evidence checklist. I'll prepare the one-page stance and a tracked-snippet file by Monday EOD (22 Jun). If procurement insists on the July 2 timeline, we can push a minimal follow-up call to finalize open points.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Legal Counsel, Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_sccs_snippet.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:15:00 +02:00
Subject: Proposed responses to Orbit MSA/DPA redline (summary)

Hi Elena — thanks for the redline and patience while we reviewed. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's proposed approach; Monica will share tracked snippets to the Drive folder linked below by Monday. Please review and confirm whether these points address Orbit counsel's concerns so we can get into a short legal-to-legal review.

1) SCCs: we will include the most recent EU SCCs as an exhibit and add a short routing fallback clause: cross-border transfers only where (i) a Transfer Impact Addendum is executed, or (ii) a documented routing exception is approved by both parties.

2) Roles & Subprocessors: Redwood remains processor for customer data under the DPA. We propose quarterly published subprocessor list + prior notice for material changes. For EU-resident data, we commit to notify and provide a 30-day window for material objections; we will not accept blocking language that halts our operational patching or urgent security work.

3) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): we propose a one-page TIA appendix that defaults hosting to EU regions for EU customers, and allows exceptions via documented sign-off with a 90-day transition window to minimize service disruption.

4) Evidence & KMS: we can provide the standard evidence package (SOC2 summary, encryption at rest docs). For customers requiring customer-managed KMS, that remains an enterprise add-on — we'll note that in the Order Form options.

Next steps:
- Monica will upload tracked DPA snippets to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfghi-orbit-dpa
- Ben, please confirm commercial timing and whether procurement can accept a short TIA appendix to enable July 2 signature.

If that is agreeable, we'll propose a 30-minute legal-to-legal call for Tue 23 Jun to close remaining items.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-4821
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@orbit-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Proposed responses to Orbit MSA/DPA redline (summary)

Karthik/Monica — thanks for the quick review and for the proposed language. High-level response:

- SCCs exhibit + the fallback language you proposed should work for our counsel, provided the TIA contains a clearer statement that customer consent is required for any transfer outside EU by default.
- Subprocessor cadence + 30-day object window for material changes is acceptable. Please make sure the tracked language clarifies what constitutes a "material" change (security/hosting/backend infra).
- For KMS: Orbit prefers customer-managed keys for the subset of EU PII we process; can you confirm the commercial terms and whether that would require an order-form add-on?

We're broadly aligned. We'll wait for the tracked snippets and a proposed Tue 23 Jun legal call time. If Redwood can commit to the TIA appendix approach and provide the standard evidence package by Mon EOD, procurement will proceed toward the July 2 target.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations
Orbit Analytics
